reader.requirement: At 85 the leftmost character of a printable item is placed in print-line column integer-1 of its COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1 clause (column 1 the leftmost, GR4), for every printable item category (VALUE, SOURCE, SUM; alphanumeric, numeric edited, signed). The witness covers literal VALUE items.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry report-multi-column-2002 (minimum 2002): at 85 refuses the multiple, relative PLUS, LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT and COL/COLS/COLUMNS/NUMBERS forms (COBOL0900); the 85 form COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1 passes
IntegerOperandRules.Classify(ctx, edition.DialectLevel): COLUMN 0 is refused at 85 citing §1985:III.2 (an integer must not be zero)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition/Year/DialectLevel in ReportWriterEmitter.EmitFieldPlacements, ReportColumnSpec.AbsoluteLeftmost and CobolReport.Place: none; the 85 form reaches AbsoluteLeftmost's default arm (= integer-1), the same code 2023 runs for an unaligned or LEFT column
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: 85 has only COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1; the 2002+ relative, multiple and aligned forms are refused at 85; placement of the 85 form is identical
reader.witnesses-cover: part: VALUE literals (g85_f30_01, g85_z01); not SOURCE edited or signed items, nor a far-right column

probes.printed: ' XYZ' / 'Q1  AB      -  5 *' / 'L1' / '   L2   007' / '  Z' (SOURCE X(6) at col 5, -ZZ9 of -5 at col 12, ALL '*' at col 17, VALUE SPACE at col 1)
probes.expected: each item's first character at its COLUMN integer

probes.printed: COBOL2386 COLUMN 0: the integer operand 0 shall be nonzero (§1985:III.2)
probes.expected: refused: an integer must not be zero

probes.printed: COBOL0900 the RIGHT alignment word requires COBOL-2002; COLPL (PLUS 2) and COLMU (COLUMNS 2 6) likewise
probes.expected: the 85 format is COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1 only; refused

reader.notes: The emitter places each item at AbsoluteLeftmost (= integer-1 for the unaligned 85 form) and Place writes from index column-1. Probes over alphanumeric, numeric-edited, signed-separate, ALL-literal and wide columns all land at their integer.
